title: Euclid I.5 angle-pair constructor with shared endpoint identities
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. Euclid I.5 supplies a complete finite construction in which equal sides, an auxiliary cut and two SAS congruences derive both equal interior base angles and equal exterior angles. This is distinct from the retained I.1 equilateral construction.

source.source_span: complete proposition statement and demonstration; source page lines 5-37 in the accessed HTML
source.source_limit: public translated edition; no claim about a specific medieval witness or target Vorlage

steps: GIVEN triangle ABC with AB=AC; EXTEND AB to D and AC to E
CHOOSE F on BD; CUT AG from AE with AG=AF; JOIN FC and GB
SAS(BFC,CGB) using BF=CG, FC=GB, common BC derives FBC=GCB and BCF=CBG
SUBTRACT equal inner pieces from equal whole angles to derive ABC=ACB; retain FBC=GCB

consequence: One shared equal-side input must yield both interior and exterior angle equalities through the same auxiliary endpoint identities. A flat equal-side classifier can predict the interior result but cannot derive the exterior result.
rival: R-I5-flat: AB=AC -> base-angle equality with exterior equality left unbound.
missing_target_binding: No target point, segment, angle, or diagram meaning is claimed. A later writer would need all auxiliary roles globally visible and no nearest-point repairs.
likely_failure: No independently owned target relation may expose the auxiliary cut, two congruence steps, and paired interior/exterior conclusions; this is then an untestable exploratory constructor, not a source failure.
